episodes.title: He Grew Up in a Cult. Chess Made Him Feel Special | Danny Rensch | UNMASKED by Olga Karpman
episodes.description:
Growing up in a cult, Danny Rensch found something in chess that his childhood couldn't give him: a sense of belonging, purpose, and self-worth.

👉 Curious which mask you want to look at? → https://olgakarpman.com/7masks

In this episode of @Unmasked.OlgaKarpman  , filmed at @websummit  Vancouver, Olga Karpman sits down with @danielrensch  , co-founder and Chief Chess Officer of Chess.com @chess  . Danny opens up about growing up in a spiritual commune he would later recognize as a cult, and how discovering chess at nine years old transformed his identity.

What began as a passion quickly became something much bigger. As Danny's talent grew, so did his status within the group. Chess gave him recognition, a sense of purpose, and the feeling that he mattered. But it also created a deeper struggle: his self-worth became inseparable from his success as a chess player.

Looking back, Danny reflects on the complicated reality of his upbringing. The same environment that exposed him to unhealthy dynamics also shaped a mindset that encouraged him to pursue what he loved. Rather than experiencing a sudden escape, he gradually became aware of the world around him and learned to navigate what he describes as living within the eye of the hurricane.

What happens when the one thing that makes you feel valuable becomes the very thing your identity depends on?

episodes.title: Raised in a Cult, Became a Chess Master—and Had to Find Himself Again | Danny Rensch | Olga Karpman
episodes.description:
🎭 A chess prodigy built his entire identity around the game. When that identity collapsed, he had to discover who he was beyond the board. In this conversation, he shares what came next.
👉Curious which mask you want to look at? → https://olgakarpman.com/7masks

In this episode of @Unmasked.OlgaKarpman  filmed at @websummit  Vancouver, Olga Karpman sits down with @danielrensch co-founder and Chief Chess Officer of Chess.com (@chess ). Danny shares how, at age 12, he was separated from his mother by a cult leader who believed he could become a world chess champion. 

He was told that chess was his spiritual destiny. He spent years believing his value was strictly tied to his performance, eventually spiraling when he failed to become a world champion. This conversation explores how that intense pressure created a fractured sense of self-worth that bled into his marriage and daily life.

He eventually realized that his identity crisis was not a failure of talent, but a misunderstanding of his own motivation. By rebuilding his relationship with his mother and separating his value from his accolades, he found a new way to engage with the world. This discussion is for anyone who has ever felt defined by their achievements and is ready to pursue authentic personal growth.

Rather than walking away from chess, he was able to find a different reason to choose it again—not simply as an achievement, but as a way to connect people, teach, serve, and create shared experiences.

When the titles, accomplishments, and masks come off—who are you underneath?
